question: A patient who received streptokinase for a previous MI should receive alteplase (not streptokinase again) for a new STEMI, because prior exposure generates neutralising antibodies that abolish streptokinase efficacy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Streptokinase is immunogenic. Prior exposure → neutralising antibodies → dramatically reduced efficacy on re-administration. This is why only non-antigenic agents (alteplase, tenecteplase) should be used after prior streptokinase therapy.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Streptokinase is a bacterial-derived protein that is strongly antigenic. A single exposure generates persistent anti-streptokinase antibodies lasting ≥5 years that neutralise subsequent doses, rendering repeat streptokinase ineffective. In addition, allergic reactions (including anaphylaxis) are more likely with re-exposure. Alteplase, tenecteplase, or reteplase (non-antigenic, recombinant tPA-based agents) are safe to use regardless of prior streptokinase exposure.
